title: Personal Financial Literacy: Taxes, Income and Budgets
seo_title: Grade 5 Personal Financial Literacy Worksheets: Taxes, Income and Budgets (TEKS 5.10, STAAR)
standard_text: 5.10A define income tax, payroll tax, sales tax, and property tax; 5.10B explain the difference between gross income and net income; 5.10C identify the advantages and disadvantages of different methods of payment, including check, credit card, debit card, and electronic payments; 5.10D develop a system for keeping and using financial records; 5.10E describe actions that might be taken to balance a budget when expenses exceed income; 5.10F balance a simple budget
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 personal financial literacy worksheets for Texas TEKS 5.10: types of taxes, gross and net income, payment methods, financial records and balancing a budget. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Net income = gross income − taxes. Balance a budget so income covers expenses.
key_sub: Debit spends your money; credit borrows. Keep records of every deposit and payment.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Taxes: income tax (on earnings), payroll tax (from paychecks, for Social Security and Medicare), sales tax (on things you buy) and property tax (on homes and land).
  • Gross income is all you earn. Net income is what is left after taxes: net = gross − taxes.
  • Ways to pay: cash, check, debit card (your money), credit card (borrowed money) and electronic payments.
  • Keep records of deposits and payments. A budget is balanced when income covers expenses.

Examples

Example

Gross income $2,400. Taxes $360.

Net = gross − taxes

$2,400 − $360

Answer: $2,040

Example

Income $500. Expenses $540.

$540 − $500 = $40 over

Cut $40 from fun or earn $40 more

Answer: balanced

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Mixing up gross and net incomeGross is before taxes; net is take-home pay.
Thinking a credit card is your own moneyA credit card is a loan you must pay back.
Adding expenses to incomeSubtract expenses from income to see what is left.

faq.a: Defining income, payroll, sales and property taxes; gross and net income; payment methods; financial records; and balancing a simple budget.

faq.q: Does Texas have a state income tax?
faq.a: No. Texans pay federal income tax but no state income tax. Texas has sales and property taxes.

faq.q: What is the difference between a debit card and a credit card?
faq.a: A debit card spends money already in your bank account. A credit card borrows money you must pay back.

faq.q: What does it mean to balance a budget?
faq.a: Make sure income is equal to or more than expenses, by spending less, earning more or both.

items.q: Which tax helps pay for Social Security?
items.e: Payroll tax pays for Social Security and Medicare.

items.q: Maya buys a backpack and pays a little more than the price on the tag. Why?
items.e: Sales tax is added when you buy something.

items.q: What is sales tax?
c: A tax added to the price of things you buy
A tax on houses and land
items.e: Sales tax is added when you buy goods. In Texas the state rate is 6.25%, and cities can add more.

items.q: The price of a video game is $40. The sales tax is $2.40. What is the total cost?
The Garcia family pays a tax each year on their house in Austin. What kind of tax is it?
items.e: A tax on a house is a property tax.

items.q: What is property tax?
c: A tax taken from a paycheck for Social Security
A tax on land and buildings that people own
items.e: Property tax is paid by owners of homes and land. It helps pay for schools and roads.

items.q: Property taxes in Texas help pay for which of these?

What is one advantage of a debit card?
c: You can spend more than you have
You spend only money you have, so you do not get into debt
items.e: A debit card spends only money in your account.

items.q: Which payment method takes money straight from your bank account when you swipe it?
items.e: A debit card uses money already in your bank account.

items.q: What is one disadvantage of a credit card?
c: Money comes out of your account right away
Interest can make things cost more if you do not pay the bill in full
It cannot be used at stores
items.e: Interest is charged on unpaid credit card balances.

items.q: What is one advantage of a credit card?
c: You can buy something now and pay for it later
items.e: A credit card lets you pay later, but you must pay the bill.

items.q: Which is an electronic payment?
c: Paying a bill online with a bank app
items.e: Paying through an app or website is an electronic payment.

items.q: What is one advantage of electronic payments?
c: They are fast and leave a record of each payment
They can only be used for groceries
items.e: Electronic payments are quick and keep a record.

items.q: What is one disadvantage of paying with a check?
c: It can take days to clear, and some stores do not accept checks
It can only be used online
items.e: Checks are slow to clear and are not accepted everywhere.

items.q: Why should a person keep a credit card bill low?

What is true about a credit card?
c: It uses money you already have in the bank
It is the same as cash
You never have to pay the money back
You borrow money and must pay it back later, sometimes with interest
items.e: A credit card is a loan. If you do not pay the full bill on time, you pay interest.

items.q: Grace has $285 in a bank account. She pays $68 for shoes with a debit card. How much is left in the account?
items.e: A debit card takes money from the account right away: $285 − $68 = $217.

items.q: Mr. Nguyen has $573 in checking. He writes a check for $76 to pay a plumber. What will his balance be after the check clears?
items.e: When the check clears, $76 leaves the account: $573 − $76 = $497.
